    How this works
    

      
The text is handed to the browser's own XML parser, the same one it uses for real documents, and
        then walked node by node to write it back out with indentation. That means well-formedness is judged
        by a real parser rather than by pattern matching: a missing close tag, a stray &, a
        second root element or a mismatched name is reported with the line and column the parser stopped at,
        and the line itself is printed with a caret under the spot. XML is case-sensitive and every tag must
        close, so <BR> and <br> are different elements and neither may
        stand alone.

      
Only the whitespace between elements is touched — the line breaks and indentation of the layout
        itself. Anything holding text, text mixed with child elements, or nothing but whitespace is written
        out on one line exactly as it came in, because in XML those spaces are part of the content and a
        formatter that reflows them changes the document: <b>  </b>
        survives both indenting and minifying. Strictly speaking the whitespace between elements is content
        too, and only a DTD or schema can say it is ignorable; that is the one liberty a formatter takes,
        and it is the reason indented XML and minified XML are both readable at all. Comments, processing
        instructions, CDATA sections and attribute order are kept. Attribute values are re-quoted with
        double quotes and their special characters escaped, which is what the serializer does; empty
        elements come back in the short <name/> form.

      
What the page does not do: it does not validate against a DTD or schema, it does not resolve
        external entities or fetch anything a DOCTYPE points at, and it does not reformat
        namespaces or rewrite prefixes. Well-formed is not the same as valid — a document can be perfectly
        well-formed and still break the schema it claims to follow. Input is capped at 2 MB; past that the
        page refuses rather than lock the tab.

      
Everything happens in this tab. Nothing is uploaded and nothing you paste is stored; the Dark and language buttons keep their own settings in this browser's local storage.
